mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% over a three-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which triggers a shift in investor sentiment toward defensive equities and reduces forward S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which leads to lower corporate earnings expectations and negative forward S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate, indicates a supply-side contraction in the real economy, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO is below its 12-month MA and UNRATE exceeds 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over a single month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which raises the cost of capital and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative forward S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in months where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with rising industrial production, indicates strong aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive forward S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS above 12-month MA and INDPRO above 108.0 fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month, sustained over two consecutive months, signals a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative forward S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated rate hikes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.0% annualized in the most recent quarter signals a weakening economy, which triggers risk-off behavior and negative forward S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 growth falls below 1.0% annualized (t-test p > 0.05).
